solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: (& 25dn.) His main concern being the NHS, Corbyn, for one, will have nurses initially stuck in basic accommodation

definitions.text: His main concern being the NHS

indicators.note: 'for one' marks the name as one example of a wider class of people sharing it
'initially' means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted
something stuck in a place is lodged inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the first name of Labour politician Jeremy Corbyn
a hut is a simple, basic shelter
first letter of nurses

explanation.surface: A politician, Corbyn, pledges to put nurses on the wards despite their poor housing.
explanation.walkthrough: Corbyn is only an example of a Jeremy; the man defined is a different Jeremy entirely. Jeremy Hunt was the UK Health Secretary for six years, responsible for the National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: As Health Secretary, the politician's ministerial brief was running Britain's National Health Service.

clue.text: (& 16dn.) Maybe Sean's getting shafted by contrary accountants

blocks.note: Sean Bean is an example of someone surnamed Bean
counter means opposite or contrary
the possessive ending supplies its letter, added at the end

explanation.surface: The actor Sean Bean is being cheated by perverse accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean Bean is an English actor famous for his characters getting killed off. 'Bean counters' is a slangy, mildly scornful term for accountants.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean counter is informal, dismissive slang for a financial clerk obsessed with tallying small sums.

clue.text: Head upset: "House belittled May – that is conviviality?"

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top
to belittle is to make small, and the smallest the word can be is its first letter

blocks.note: nob is slang for the head
HO is the standard abbreviation for house
the month cut down to its initial
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A headline: the Commons sneered at Theresa May, asking whether that counts as friendliness.
explanation.walkthrough: May reads as Theresa May, the Prime Minister being belittled in the House of Commons; here it is just a word to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is a French borrowing meaning cheerful, friendly good nature among company.

clue.text: G-spot? It lies not quite askew, somewhere in the throat

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter
askew means crooked or out of line, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, without the hyphen
taken as written
the word minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A smutty question about where the G-spot is, answered with a coy evasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a search somewhere much lower; the letters of G-spot, it and a shortened lies are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is a flap of cartilage at the back of the throat covering the windpipe during swallowing.

clue.text: British in infernal place – Cyclops makes for an Italian port

blocks.note: Br is an abbreviation for British
taken as written
Dis is the classical name for the underworld, or Dante's city of hell
the setter, Cyclops, refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A Briton stuck somewhere hellish, while the setter heads off to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but is simply its own two letters. A setter's pseudonym stands for the first-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Brindisi is a seaport on the Adriatic coast in Puglia, southern Italy.

clue.text: Hello? Gutless bloke covers shortfall

indicators.note: having no guts means losing the insides, so the middle letter goes
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes on the outside

blocks.note: a guy is a bloke, a man
a shortfall is a deficit or loss

explanation.surface: Someone answering the phone, a spineless man who makes up a deficit.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! looks like a greeting but is the British celebrity magazine; the question mark flags it as an example of a type.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper, and the celebrity weekly is a classic instance.

clue.text: Shelter provided by area of golf course when taking a piss

blocks.note: the tee is where each hole is played from
a pee is a piss, an act of urinating

explanation.surface: A golfer seeks cover on the course while relieving themself.
explanation.walkthrough: The golfing scene suggests a hut or bunker, but the shelter is a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A teepee is a conical tent of skins or canvas used by Plains peoples of North America.

clue.text: Wind up drunk with elastic/nylon tops

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, so each word gives its opener

blocks.note: tight is informal for drunk
first letters of elastic and nylon

explanation.surface: Ending up intoxicated while wearing stretchy synthetic tops.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind up reads as ending up, and tops as garments; both have other jobs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding a spring or a clock key screws it tauter, which is what tightening means.

clue.text: Hitler didn't quite rise to this crop-twirling sort of sex

definitions.text: Hitler didn't quite rise to this

indicators.note: twirling spins things round, so these letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before being rearranged
oral sex is one kind

explanation.surface: A lurid claim about the dictator's kinky tastes involving a riding crop.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitler served in the First World War as a Gefreiter, roughly a lance corporal, so he never quite made full corporal. A crop is a short riding whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank above lance corporal is the one Hitler is often loosely credited with but never actually held.

clue.text: see 20dn.
Political supporter – hag! – has no time for London borough

indicators.note: having none of something means going without it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a Green supports the Green Party
a hag is an ugly old woman, a witch
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A party activist insults an old woman who won't make time for her borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the borough losing time is home to Greenwich Mean Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich is a borough of south-east London on the Thames, site of the Royal Observatory.

clue.text: John comes by squeezing nuts at first

indicators.note: to squeeze something is to hold it tightly inside, so one piece goes around another
at first points to the beginning, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: to come by something is to obtain or get it
first letter of nuts

explanation.surface: A man named John drops in and grabs someone's testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: John is not a man's name but American slang for a toilet; the Gents is the British term for a men's lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a toilet, the latter specifically the men's public lavatory in Britain.

clue.text: Date? Have a bash, by the way

blocks.note: to have a bash is to have a try
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone, as an aside, suggests giving a romantic date a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' reads as an idle aside, but 'by' joins the pieces and 'the way' is the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret romantic meeting arranged between lovers, a kind of date.

clue.text: Luvvie-like Rachel at it, indiscriminately

indicators.note: doing something indiscriminately means without order or care, so the letters fall at random

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An actressy Rachel is having sex with anyone at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Luvvie is British slang for a gushing, self-important actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical describes the exaggerated, showy manner associated with stage performers and their gushing affectation.

clue.text: Article: "May's number 1 involved with doom in financial quarter"

indicators.note: the number one position in a word is its opening letter
involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: first letter of May
taken as written
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A news piece about Theresa May's chief aide mixed up in a City disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 1' suggests May's top adviser, but it just picks her first letter. The City is London's Square Mile, its banking district.
explanation.definitionFit: A commodity is a tradeable good or product, an article in the sense of an item for sale.

clue.text: Foreign telecaster's unit that's subject of token closure by Kim Jong-un?

definitions.text: subject of token closure by Kim Jong-un?

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so these letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An overseas broadcaster's crew is the target of a symbolic shutdown by North Korea's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2018 North Korea staged the demolition of its Punggye-ri test facility for foreign journalists, which critics called a token gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Kim's regime publicly blew up the tunnels where it detonated its atomic bombs, a largely symbolic act.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Spots caused by dodgy Iran dive?

definitions.note: plural noun defining a mass noun: spots of rain

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so these letters are not to be taken straight

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a dive is a plunge or fall

explanation.surface: Skin blemishes blamed on a dubious plunge in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: Spots suggests pimples, but here it means spots of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Light rain is described as spots or spitting, so drops of precipitation make up the fall.

clue.text: Sex tremendous, not entirely intense

indicators.note: not the whole of the words is used, only a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters starting after the opening S

explanation.surface: A review of a sexual encounter: great, but not completely passionate.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts one letter into the first word and stops before the end of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something at a very high degree or severity, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: In a shit position, being a resident without entitlement?

blocks.note: first meaning: crouching on the heels, the posture for relieving oneself
second meaning: occupying a building without legal right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shit position' sounds like slang for being in trouble, but it is literal: the crouch used for defecating.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both crouching low on one's heels and occupying an empty property illegally.

clue.text: Corporation excess reduced by such exercises?

definitions.text: Corporation excess reduced by such exercises?

blocks.note: surface reading: a company trimming its surplus
setter's reading: an old jokey word for a pot belly, whose fat these exercises work off

explanation.walkthrough: Corporation suggests a business cutting costs, but it is dated British slang for a large paunch, so the excess is belly fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal exercises lifting the torso from lying flat are what people do to trim a paunch.

clue.text: (& 9dn.) Being old, Di scarcely hides record success

indicators.note: to hide something is to conceal it inside, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the words from the end of the first

explanation.surface: An ageing Diana conceals how well her recordings sold.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase straddles Being, old, Di and scarcely; the comma does not interrupt it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold disc is an award certifying that a record has sold a large number of copies.

clue.text: Labour leader involved in fight makes a half-soaked impact

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the first letter is wanted
to be involved in something is to be inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a spat is a petty quarrel or fight
first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: The head of the Labour Party, caught up in a row, makes a damp landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' suggests the party's head, Corbyn, but it is only an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the wet slapping noise of something soft hitting a surface, halfway to a splash.

clue.text: Pictures here of illicit lover grabbing Trudeau's rear

indicators.note: to grab is to take hold of and clutch, so one piece wraps around another
the rear of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written; illicit only colours the surface
last letter of Trudeau

explanation.surface: Photos of a secret paramour groping the Canadian prime minister's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Pictures suggests scandalous photos, but means paintings, and 'here' points to where they hang.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris art museum houses paintings such as the Mona Lisa, so it is a place for pictures.

clue.text: Tsk! One time back passage involving all the players

indicators.note: going back means heading the opposite way, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: tsk and tut are both sounds of disapproval
the Roman numeral for one
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Disapproval of a past episode of anal sex involving the whole team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back passage' and 'players' push a crude reading; 'back' reverses and the passage is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, tutti is an Italian marking for a section played by the whole orchestra together.

clue.text: Complete set of bloated politicians in session

blocks.note: bloated means stuffed or full
a parliamentary chamber sitting, such as the House of Commons

explanation.surface: A cynical description of a whole chamber of overfed MPs sitting together.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a gaming phrase: in bingo or housey-housey a full house is the whole card completed.
explanation.definitionFit: In bingo and similar games, crossing off every number on the card means a winning full card.

clue.text: see 1dn.
Drink, large, imbibed by former president (easily carried away)

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in, so one piece is swallowed inside another

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
Abe is Abraham Lincoln
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big drink swallowed by an ex-president who gets a bit carried away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easily carried away' sounds like someone overexcited, but it means light enough to carry off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something portable is light or compact enough to be moved by hand without difficulty.

clue.text: Trump reaction to any critical news item? "Turn off! EU involved!"

definitions.text: Trump reaction to any critical news item?
definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for the adjective he applies

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of kilter, so the letters are put out of order
involved means mixed in and tangled, so the added letters join the jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Trump's response to hostile coverage: switch it off, the Europeans are behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn off reads as a command to switch off the television, but turn is fodder and off scrambles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump habitually dismissed unfavourable reporting as fake news, meaning false and not factual.
